subject: Anthropology
title: Ethnography
description: A fast breakdown of Ethnography for builders.

hook.text: An ethnography is more than a report. It's a detailed portrait of how a group of people live and think.

buildup.text: Ethnography is both method and product: the process of fieldwork and the written account that results.

discovery.text: Good ethnography captures voices, tensions, humor, and contradiction — not just abstract social structures.

twist.text: Writing ethnography is itself political. Whose story gets told, and how, reflects the author's own power and bias.

climax.text: Ethnography is anthropology's core contribution: rich, deep accounts of human life that no other method matches.

punchline.text: The best science sometimes reads like literature.

quiz.question: What makes ethnography distinctive?
options: It produces rich, deep accounts of how people live and think

details.summary: Ethnography is both the primary research method and the written product of cultural anthropology. It involves extended immersive fieldwork in a community followed by detailed descriptive and analytical writing. Good ethnography conveys the lived experience of a cultural world from the inside.
details.whyItMatters: Ethnography produces the deep, contextual understanding that distinguishes anthropology from other disciplines. No survey or experiment captures what extended immersion reveals about how people experience their lives, make meaning.
takeaways: Ethnography is both a research method and a written product
It requires extended immersive fieldwork in a community
It produces deep contextual understanding of lived experience

faq.question: How long does ethnographic fieldwork typically last?
faq.answer: Traditional fieldwork lasts at least one year to capture seasonal cycles and establish deep relationships. Modern constraints and new research contexts have produced shorter fieldwork periods.

faq.question: How is ethnography different from journalism?
faq.answer: Ethnography requires extended immersion, participant observation, theoretical framing, and reflexive analysis of the researcher's position. Journalism is typically shorter, more event-driven, and less theoretically engaged.
